**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject runs with failed live writes**

When a preliminary GET fails, a PATCH returns non-200, or a 200 response cannot be decoded, the write is omitted from `Expected`; the verdict checks only delivered observations and observer attachment, not `WritesAnswered == WritesAsked`. Consequently, a run with fewer than the required 200 writes and 10,000 observations can still report plain `"met"`. Treat every unsent or unsuccessful write as a failed expected observation and prevent a passing verdict.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject samples whose response body was incomplete**

When a response returns 2xx headers and `io.ReadAll` subsequently fails, `client.do` stores the failure in `apiSample.Err`, but this branch still adds its server and partial round-trip times to the successful sample set. A run containing truncated focus, task, table, graph, or write responses can therefore report a target as `met`; treat a nonempty `s.Err` as a failed attempt and exclude it from the latency distribution.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not reuse a later arrival for multiple writes**

When the writable-task sequence revisits a task and an observer misses an earlier invalidation, the same later arrival satisfies every preceding write because it is never consumed and `a.Version >= w.Version`. Since these writes toggle state, an arrival for a later `todo` version can falsely count as delivery of an earlier `doing` write that was never observed, allowing all expected observations and a passing verdict despite a missing update. Match each arrival to at most one write, or verify the expected state/version for each write.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Scope candidate verification to the material change**

A valid material change will then be classified as `unverified` whenever unrelated candidates make `added != total`, preventing the material target from passing under the intended concurrent workload; count only `flow_source_changed` candidates attributable to this change or its supporter tasks.

When a focus refetch lasts until the next invalidation batch—possible with the default 1.5-second write interval even near the 2-second target—`flush` clears `timer` before doing its network reads, so the next event starts another `AfterFunc` callback and refetch concurrently. The real client serializes these refreshes through `LiveBus.run` and `useFlowTable`'s `serial` queue; allowing the harness's second refetch to bypass the first can make later observations complete much earlier and produce a passing p95 that the client would miss. Keep the batch marked as running and queue one follow-up flush instead.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub> Security: Bound Flow audit fan-out per request**

When Flow is enabled, an ordinary member can prepare 100 owned focuses with 200 tasks each and repeatedly request `/api/v1/flow/table?limit=100`. This new loop converts that one read token into at least 41 separate `Guard.Release` calls; each opens/commits a transaction and appends a 500-item audit row. The default limiter permits 600 reads/minute plus a 100-request burst per replica, while these rows are append-only and retained for a year, so a member can monopolize the API DB pool and grow durable audit storage until OKR is unavailable. Production is currently default-off, so impact is conditional, but staging is on. Cap total items/batches per response or charge limits by audited items.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Drain in-flight requests before ending measurement**

When a session starts its final request shortly before `end`, this deadline cancels the request exactly at the measurement boundary; because its `Sent` timestamp is still before `end`, the canceled request is retained as a measured failure. With 50 randomly phased sessions, requests whose legitimate latency overlaps the cutoff can therefore make an otherwise valid run permanently `incomplete, not met`, since every target requires zero failures. Stop scheduling new work at `end`, but allow already-started requests to finish under the caller's context before building the report.
